## Architecture Style

**Modular Monolith · VSA + CQS · DDD** — a single deployable unit partitioned into independently cohesive modules (`Todos`, `Notifications`); features are organised as vertical slices (one folder per use case) rather than horizontal layers; all state mutations go through commands and all reads through queries (CQS), mediated by MediatR.

## Key Patterns

- **Vertical Slice Architecture (VSA)** — each feature owns its full stack under `Application/Features/<Entity>/<Commands|Queries|Events>/`; no shared application-layer base classes
- **CQS via MediatR** — `ICommand<TResult>` / `IQuery<TResult>` from `BuildingBlocks`; pipeline behaviours for logging, validation, and tracing
- **DDD Rich Aggregates** — domain entities encapsulate invariants and raise domain events from inside the aggregate (e.g., `Todo.CompleteTodo()` raises `TodoCompletedEvent`)
- **Domain Events** — raised via `BaseEntity.Raise()`; dispatched post-EF `SaveChanges` to the internal event bus
- **CAP + RabbitMQ (Integration Events)** — cross-module async messaging through DotNetCore.CAP; contracts in `src/Contracts/` only
- **EF Core (commands)** — primary ORM for write paths and schema migrations
- **Dapper (queries)** — used for complex read paths and reporting where EF generates suboptimal SQL
- **MediatR Pipeline Behaviours** — `ValidationBehavior`, `LoggingBehavior`, `ActivityBehavior` applied globally
- **SignalR** — real-time push from `Notifications` module via `TodoHub`

## Layering Rules

```
Domain  ←  Application  ←  Infrastructure  ←  Api (Presentation)
                ↑
         BuildingBlocks (leaf — no module references)
         Contracts     (leaf — integration events only)
```

**Hard rules:**
- `Domain` has zero external dependencies — no EF Core, no MediatR, no framework attributes
- `Application` references `Domain` and `BuildingBlocks` only; never `Infrastructure` directly
- `Infrastructure` implements interfaces declared in `Application`; it is never referenced upward
- `Api` wires modules and maps HTTP requests; it references `Application` only (never `Domain` or `Infrastructure` directly)
- Cross-module communication MUST go through `Contracts` events + CAP message bus — no direct assembly references between `Todos` and `Notifications`
- `BuildingBlocks` and `Contracts` are leaves; they MUST NOT reference any module
- Architecture rules are enforced by `tests/ArchTests/` (ArchUnit.NET) — violations break the build
